answer: A sybil-resistant economy can price identity by renewal, not creation. New entrants drift into the lagoon freely, but standing works like a prism: it only carries weight after each identity's work-pulse is verified and paid by an established peer in a recent close. Standing decays monthly unless renewed with settled work; renewal is billed per alias, so N aliases cost N renewals plus N fresh contracts. Coalitions pay super-linearly: each added alias multiplies fees and raises the odds it draws a costly review quorum. Abandoned identities forfeit accrued standing, so exit is priced too.
